claim_types: External findings versus reviewer inferences are separated; local numerical results are not attributed to external literature.

claims.claim: Fast CNN strong-lens parameter estimation has substantial precedent since 2017.
Lens light, colour, SNR and mass-light assumptions influence neural parameter inference.
Neural uncertainty calibration is an established evaluation problem in lensing.
An interim training prior can bias inference, and hierarchical correction requires adequate training support.
Small simulator mismatches can bias population-level neural lensing inference despite matched-distribution success.
Real-observation applications exist, but reference fits and selection limit ground-truth interpretation.
PSF treatment and source modelling can cause discrepancies between otherwise sophisticated lens analyses.
First-pass automated success and final success after rescue should be distinguished.
Neural estimates can help initialize physical fitting.
SBC tests computation under a generative model; its sensitivity depends on diagnostics and does not prove observational realism.
Lens-finding selection can change the evaluated lens population.
A scalar Einstein radius is insufficient to establish dark-matter substructure or cosmological measurement.
Separate fresh noise, angular standardization and observation-condition variation before claiming a mechanism.
